rhythm.value: Detector: 23 shots, 22 cuts, median 0.467 s, 128.6 cuts/min. Corrected: 19 shots, 18 cuts, median 0.30 s, 105 cuts/min over 10.27 s. The film has three speeds. (1) 0-5.77 s, the design-object section: 8 shots, median 0.60 s (0.30, 1.57, 1.13, 0.93, 0.60, 0.60, 0.20, 0.43 s); each shot is one centred object changing state inside the shot, so the eye never leaves frame centre. (2) 5.77-8.00 s, the argument: one 0.47 s outline-word card, then 9 footage shots, 8 of them 3-6 frames (0.10-0.20 s, median 0.133 s), under one caption that never moves. (3) 8.00-10.27 s: one 2.27 s hold on the mark while its backdrop dies to black. Fast-in-the-middle, still-at-the-end: the only shot over 1.6 s is the last. A second, independent clock runs over the cuts: a 3-frame navy (#021563) ground blink at F0, F62, F110, F129, F150, F157, F220, F267, F286 and a 1-frame one at F307 (last frame). Gaps 62, 48, 19, 21 | 7 | 63, 47, 19, 21 frames: the same 150-frame (5.0 s) figure runs twice, offsets 0, 62, 110, 129, 150 then 157, 220, 267, 286, 307. SOUND WAS NOT HEARD, and here there is nothing to hear: audio.json reports one silence span 0-10.325 s, no onsets, loudness range 0 LU, and sync.json carries only cutCount 22. No tempo, so cutsOnBeatRatio/cutsOnBeatChance, cutsOnOnsetRatio/cutsOnOnsetChance and every v2 lift figure cannot be computed: there is no evidence either way about picture-to-music sync. The Whisper word 'you' at 0-2.06 s is a hallucination on silence and is rejected. The repeating blink figure is the strongest hint that the original cut was made to a music phrase that this file does not carry (this clause alone is inferred, confidence 0.4).

value.name: polarity-strobe-title
value.description: Full-frame flashes in 3-frame blocks (navy F0-F2, black F3-F5, white F6-F8), then a tiny white sentence centred on black at F11 (OCR box 25% width, 7% height). The whole frame inverts every 7 frames: white ground with a faint tinted title F16-F22, black again F23 with an RGB-split smear F24-F25, clean F26. Then nothing moves for 21 frames (F26-F46, 0.70 s). Exit: the type flares green with a glow for 2 frames (F47-F48) and is gone at F49; 7 black frames before the next object.
value.why: The flashes buy attention without content, then the type is so small in so much black that the eye must go to centre and read; the long still hold after the strobe makes the claim feel settled. The flare exit is a full stop, not a fade.

value.name: icon-swell-to-ground
value.description: A gradient pill (about 68% width) recolours (F59), shrinks (F61), blinks navy (F62-F64) and leaves only its 4%-wide icon (F65). Two frames of stillness, then a violet disc grows out of the icon F68-F75, slow then fast: about 8% width at F68, 14% at F71, 25% at F73, full frame height at F74, the ground by F75. Fitted curve on this push: expo.in-like bezier (0.562, 0.338, 0.88, -0.462).
value.why: The eye has been parked on frame centre by the title; the object arrives exactly there, collapses to its smallest form and then becomes the whole frame, so the next scene grows out of the last one with no cut.

value.name: word-becomes-shape
value.description: Hard cut to one small lowercase word in a magenta-to-violet gradient, centred (F90). Held 5 frames. F95-F98 its letters scatter vertically (one letter rises, two drop); F99-F101 all but the first letter fade; F102-F107 the remaining upright stroke stands alone and lengthens; F108-F113 it rotates to about 35 degrees off vertical and grows to about 46% of frame height, decelerating, with a navy blink F110-F112 underneath; held F113-F117. Hard cut at F118 to a lit square whose diagonal light streak runs at the same angle and position as the stroke.
value.why: The word is literally drawn by its own letter, which proves craft in 0.6 s. The streak in the next shot continues the stroke's angle, so the eye follows a diagonal across the cut and never notices it.

value.name: ground-blink-punctuation
value.description: Ten times, the black ground is replaced by flat navy #021563 for 3 frames (the last one for 1 frame) while the foreground stays put, re-rendered as pink or white halftone. Blinks at F0, F62, F110, F129, F150, F157, F220, F267, F286, F307; gaps 62, 48, 19, 21, 7, 63, 47, 19, 21 frames: one 150-frame figure played twice. Six of them sit on the last frames before a change of state (F65 icon alone, F113 stroke tilted, F132 halftone square, F160 cut, F289, end).
value.why: A ground swap is louder than any move but costs no layout: the object stays where the eye is. It works as an accent on a beat that this silent file does not carry, and as a seam that hides each state change.

value.name: caption-anchor-over-footage-stutter
value.description: One small white lowercase caption (OCR box 25% width, 6% height, centred at 0.49, 0.50) holds in exactly the same place over 9 shots of 3-6 frames each (F187-F239): archival portraits, thermal-violet footage, a desk computer, a laptop from above, a hand with a card, medical scans. Each shot carries thin tracking boxes with coordinate tags on its subject and is graded differently (scan bars, thermal violet, halftone, cold cyan). The caption swaps to its second word once, at F212, in the same position. Overexposed single frames at F211, F215, F219 punctuate.
value.why: The eye reads the fixed caption and lets the pictures flicker in the periphery, so 9 images in 1.77 s feel like one thought, not chaos. The tracking boxes make history look like data being analysed, which ties archival pictures to the design work before it.
